prompt: How many real zeros does $p(x) = (x - 1)(x - 4)(x + 3)$ have?
hint: Each factor is zero for one value of $x$. How many factors are there, and are their zeros all different?

hints.text: Each factor is zero for one value of $x$. How many factors are there, and are their zeros all different?
Set each factor to zero to get $x = 1$, $x = 4$, and $x = -3$. Check that no value repeats, then count them.
The three values are all different, so the polynomial has $3$ real zeros.

explanation: A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, so set each factor to zero in turn.
The three factors give the zeros $x = 1$, $x = 4$, and $x = -3$.
Those are $3$ different values, so there are $3$ real zeros and the graph crosses the $x$-axis $3$ times.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the crossings
steps: Imagine a wiggly track drawn across a number line.
It dives through the axis at $-3$, then at 1, then at 4.
Three dives means three real zeros.
